subject: lighthouse
pitch: A lighthouse on a tiny island.
reasoning:
I'm planning a lighthouse-on-island model where the root needs its own joint since parts require a resolvable joint hierarchy, so I'll set up a root joint at the origin. I'm thinking through efficient but visually appealing construction, using striped paint patterns for the tower and mottled textures for the rocky island base.

I'm sizing the tower around 12m tall and the island around 6m radius, with a flat teal sea disc at the base, stacked low-poly rock cylinders rising to a grass cap, scattered dodecahedron rocks around the rim, and a tapered cylindrical tower painted with clean red-and-white horizontal stripes.

Now I'm stacking the tower details upward: the gallery cylinder and corbel cone sit around y=11.3–11.95, a thin torus railing with posts rings the gallery near y=12.5, a bright yellow glass lantern room spans roughly 11.95–13.25 with dark vertical mullions, and a dark cone roof caps it off from 13.25 to 14.15.

I'm also working out the door placement at the tower's base facing forward, with a small rotated cylinder forming an arch above it, and planning how to scatter small dark window boxes spiraling up the tapering radius by computing position from angle and height using the tower's shrinking radius function.

Then I'm sizing a small keeper's cottage beside the tower, checking its corners stay within the island's grass radius, shrinking its dimensions to fit safely, and sketching out a simple four-sided cone roof for it.

Still adjusting cone geometry...

Settling on a 1.7x1.7 cottage with a 1.3-radius cone roof for slight overhang, plus a small chimney box and modest door/window. I'll skip paths and fences but add a wooden dock with planks and posts extending off the island into the sea, forgoing boats and seagulls for now.

For the tower, instead of using a built-in striped paint helper (which would wobble due to taper noise), I'm writing a custom paint function based on world y-coordinate to alternate red and white bands cleanly, with a black base band near the bottom.

For the island surfaces I'm using mottled textures—grayish for rock, green tones for grass—and scattering nine irregular icosahedron rocks around a ring near the island edge with randomized size and flattened shape. I'm also adding a few white foam torus rings in the sea near the island's base to suggest surf.

For the door, I'm positioning it on the front face of the tower, slightly offset outward on the z-axis so it protrudes naturally from the tower's curved surface at the right height. Time to write it all out.
